question_verdicts.reason: It carries the assumption at marking 0, which the gap names: an assumption with no confirmed question, and Research.md:353 makes every assumption a question to the owner. No row V1 to V264 asks it; V80 asks the forward direction only. In T1 the critic rejected this wording for leaving out the DC-input state, and the re-check rejected the critic's all-states version because the pages already state the blocking. That page statement comes from commit 8d8964f's plan, not from the owner, so it does not settle the assumption. The omitted state is covered: IOBoard.md:334 and :338 put the display on the 5 V rail made from the selected source, so with the DC input or with the pack the rail is up and faces the display's VBUS through the cable. The pack-case answer therefore holds for the DC-input case. A yes or no decides whether P2 qualifies a reverse-blocking part, so it blocks P2.

added.question: While the board runs from the 2S pack, must the source selection keep the pack's voltage off the DC input connector's pins, with the DC input unplugged or its source switched off: yes or no?
added.why: IOBoard.md:324 and Research.md:61 state only that the selection is automatic. F8 (Research.md:536, owner 2026-09-25) says the pack does not charge from the DC input, so the selection blocks current from the DC input into the pack. No page states the other direction, pack out through the DC input's pins. It decides whether P2 needs reverse blocking on the DC input's side. A reverse-polarity stage built as a series P-channel MOSFET does not block it; an ideal diode or an eFuse with reverse blocking does.
added.for_quantity: pack voltage back-fed onto the DC input connector
